newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX firmer as MOL, TVK bolsters turnover.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX firmer as MOL, TVK bolsters turnover.

text.p: Hungary's share market ended the week in an upbeat mood and spot turnover was boosted by heavily traded MOL and TVK, dealers said.
The BUX index finished at 5,703.78 points, up 41.39.
Spot share turnover surged to 4.48 billion forints from 3.37 billion on Thursday, with MOL accounting for 2.1 billion forints and TVK for 1.36 billion.

"MOL's turnover was benefiting from small shareholders' demand for it while news of a big loan for MOL had no impact," said Robert Forgo of MKB Securities. "Foreigners sell all MOL shares while local small shareholders absorb everything."
Shares of MOL which signed an $500 million, seven-year syndicated loan with a consortium of 24 banks at 30 basis points above LIBOR, closed at 3,120 forints, down 15.
MOL also said it planned to pay a 3.7 percent dividend against 0.9 percent last year.
Trading in TVK started at around Thursday's closing level before a sudden surge brought its price to a peak of 2,760 forints before retreating to close at 2,740, up 110.

"I think the price reflects hot expectations of very strong first quarter figures," Forgo said. TVK said this morning it would propose an eight percent dividend to its shareholders on the 1996 earnings.
Elsewhere on the market most issues were moving upwards as fears of a new rate hike in the U.S. seemed to have diminished.
Gas distributor Primagaz shareholders approved a 17.5 percent dividend on 1996 earnings at an annual general meeting held after the bourse's close. Primagaz closed at 12,500, up 500.
Pharmaceuticals Human, paying a 3.56 percent dividend on 1996 earnings, closed at 2,980, up 70.
